title: Materialize Config on a Packaged Ryoku Install

answer: For a packaged Ryoku install, `ryoku materialize` lays `/usr/share/ryoku/config` into `~/.config`, then overlays `~/.config/ryoku/user_edits` last. It is not the dev-checkout command: on a clone, use `ryoku deploy`. To test another base tree deliberately, set `RYOKU_CONFIG_BASE`; do not hand-copy into `~/.config` and treat that as delivery testing.

title: Deploy Custom Work From a Ryoku Checkout
examples: I cloned Ryoku and changed some QML, what is the proper way to run my work?

can I use materialize from a dev checkout?
I need to build and deploy my custom Ryoku work locally
answer: On a dev checkout, point `RYOKU_REPO` at that checkout and run `ryoku deploy`. It builds the Go binaries and QML plugin, then runs `ryoku/shell/deploy.sh` to lay the checkout into `~/.config` and records the deployed commit. `ryoku materialize` is for packaged installs and fails on a normal checkout. Deploy changes live state, so commit or stash unrelated work first and test the affected behavior afterward.

title: Verify a Ryoku Contribution Before Commit

answer: Test the behavior on the running system after `ryoku deploy`; parsing alone is not enough. For changed Lua run `luac -p <file>` and for shell scripts run `bash -n <file>`. Installer contributors can run its non-destructive matrix with `RYOKU_DRYRUN=1` and the documented strategy/profile variables. Before committing, run `bin/ryoku-dev-verify-delivery` so a user-facing config is actually delivered; keep the repo hooks enabled and never use `--no-verify`.

A development checkout is different: `ryoku update` follows its configured git channel and redeploys it. Do not use an installer/erase-disk answer for a normal update question.

Do not kill processes or edit Hermes/Rashin files blindly; the source-supported next step is the ACP health check.

title: Use a Ryoku Update Channel

answer: GUI: `Ryoku Settings > System > Updates` shows the current update state. Switching a channel is CLI/development work, not a normal Hub setting: `ryoku track main` or `ryoku track unstable-dev` creates/uses a tracked checkout and makes later `ryoku update` follow that channel. `unstable-dev` is intentionally development work and does not reach normal users until promoted to `main`; use it only if you deliberately accept branch churn. This does not require reinstalling an ISO.
